rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke targets the Quraysh deniers’ indulgent luxury, especially the Banu al-Mughira; the blame concerns luxuriating in blessings, not the blessings themselves.
rows.anchor: صفة للمكذبين وهم صناديد قريش وكانوا أهل ترفه وتنعم لا سيما بني المغيرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet warned Muadh, when appointing him governor in Yemen, against indulgence, since God’s servants are not people of luxury.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام ، لمعاذ رضي الله عنه حين بعثه إلى اليمن واليا إياك والتنعم فإن عباد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning consoles the poor: they enter Paradise five hundred years before the wealthy.
rows.anchor: وفيه تسلية للفقراء فإنهم يدخلون الجنة قبل الأغنياء بخمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants them only a brief reprieve because worldly life is short and every coming event is near; the following threats explain the reprieve.
rows.anchor: زمانا قليلا وأجلهم أجلا يسيرا ولا تعجل فإن الله سيعذبهم في الآخرة إذ عمر الدنيا قليل وكل آت قريب

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says little time separated revelation of this verse from Badr, which is why some classified the verse as Medinan.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري كان بين نزول هذه الآية ووقعة بدر زمان يسير ولذا قيل إنها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened restraints and fire are prepared realities in the afterlife, rather than merely things in God’s knowledge, making the threat more forceful; they are embodied forms of evil deeds.
rows.anchor: وفيما هيأناه للعصاة من آلات العذاب وأسبابه وهو أولى من قول بعضهم في علمنا وتقديرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy shackles bind criminals’ feet to humiliate and torment them, not to prevent escape; listing the punishments demonstrates God’s power to avenge.
rows.anchor: قيودا ثقالا يقيد بها أرجل المجرمين إهانة لهم وتعذيبا لا خوفاف من فرارهم

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf describes Jahim as a fire of extreme heat and blazing intensity.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف هي النار الشديدة الحر والاتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choking food sticks in the throat and can neither be swallowed nor expelled; the worldly plants called darīʿ and zaqqum are poisonous and repulsive, so their hellish forms are worse still.
rows.anchor: هو ما ينشب في الحلق ويعلق من عظم وغيره فلا ينساغ أي طعاما غير سائغ يأخذ بالحلق لا هو نازل ولا هو خارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned receive this food because they consumed God’s blessings while disbelieving in them; it opposes the pleasant food of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وإنما ابتلوا بهما لأنهم أكلوا نعمة الله وكفروا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite phrase “painful punishment” encompasses further kinds of torment whose measure and true nature cannot be grasped.
rows.anchor: ونوعا آخر من العذاب مؤلما لا يقادر قدره ولا يدرك كنهه كما يدل عليه التنكير

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet collapsed unconscious when this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير نه لما نزلت هذه الآية خر النبي عليه السلام مغشيا عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri repeatedly put away food while fasting after encountering this verse; visitors eventually persuaded him to drink a little sawīq.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن البصري قدس سره إنه أمسى صائما فأتى طعام

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fath al-Rahman treats the specification of dawn as an invitation to contemplate its marvels and the ordered regularity of its many motions.
rows.anchor: وفي "فتح الرحمن" تخصيص تشريف وتنبيه على النظر في عجائبه

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth explains the moon in the preceding oath as the crescent after its third night.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الليث وخالق القمر يعني الهلال بعد ثالثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night and dawn clauses are coordinated with the moon; “when” is future-looking here because dawn follows night.
rows.anchor: معطوف على القمر وكذا الصبح يعني

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes safara, uncovering a physical covering, from asfara, which describes a color becoming clear and bright.
rows.anchor: اللسفر كشف الغطاء ويختص ذلك بالأعيان نحو سفر العمامة عن الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfara means that dawn brightens and clears; “pray at isfar” can mean entering the dawn time.
rows.anchor: والصبح إذا أسفر أي أشرق لونه ووجهه وأسفروا بالفجر تؤجروا من قولهم اسفرت أي دخلت فيه

rows.speaker: قوت القلوب
rows.claim: Qut al-qulub describes the second dawn as the sun’s white glow beneath the red twilight; sunset moves from red to white and darkness, while sunrise reverses that order before the sun’s disk appears.
rows.anchor: وفي قوت القلوب الفجر الثاني هو انشقاق شفق الشمس وهو بريق بياضها الذي تحت الحمرة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi reads the moon inwardly as a receptive, clear heart, the dark night as the lower self, and dawn as spirit-light that removes the heart’s darkness.
rows.anchor: اقسم بالقمر أي بالقلب المستعد الصافي القابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakar symbolizes nature and the hell of the lower self, which explains the placement of the moon, night, and dawn imagery before its terrors.
rows.anchor: لأن سقر إشارة إلى الطبيعة وجهنم النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kibar is the plural of kubra; Sakar is one of the greatest calamities and, if understood as definite, unparalleled in its magnitude.
rows.anchor: والكبر جمع الكبرى جعت الف التأنيث كتائه وألحقت بها فكما جمعت فعلة على فعل كركبة وركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the objection concerns the number of keepers, Sakar is a major proof of God’s power to subdue sinners from Adam to the Resurrection through a small number of guards; if it concerns the signs, it is one of the greatest signs.
rows.anchor: وإن كان منكرا لعدة الخزنة فالمعنى إنها من إحدى الحجج أكبر نذيرا من قدرة الله على قهر العصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhiran is an accusative of specification: Sakar is among the greatest terrors as a warning; its masculine form is explained by construing the pronoun as punishment or as “possessing warning.”
rows.anchor: من نسبة إحدى الكبر إلى اسم أن لأن معناه إنها من معظمات الدواهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses whoever chooses to advance through good, Paradise, and obedience, or to fall behind through sin; this hints that human acquisition contributes to felicity or deprivation.
rows.anchor: نذيرا لمن شاء منكم أن يسبق إلى الخير والجنة والطاعة فيهديه الله أو لم يشأ ذلك ويتأخر بالمعصية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya interprets the moon, dark night, and white dawn as the luminous law, dark nature, and reality; people manifest one of three broad stations, and the warning urges advance to law rather than retreat to nature.
rows.anchor: اقسم بنور قمر الشريعة الزهراء وبظلمة ليل الطيعة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya says reality is the highest station, reached only by a few perfected ones, which is why it is omitted from the invitation to advance or retreat.
rows.anchor: ولما كان مقام الحقيقة أعلى المرتب ولم يصل إليه إلا النذر من الكمل أعرض عن ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who informs at the reckoning may be God, an angel acting by His command, or the record of deeds as it is unfolded.
rows.anchor: والمخبر هو الله أو الملك بأمره أو كتابه ينشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What he sent ahead” can mean any good or evil deed he performed; “what he left behind” can mean good or evil he failed to do, or deeds whose effects continued after him.
rows.anchor: أي لم يعمل خيرا كان أو شرا فيعاقب بالأول ويثاب بالثاني أو بما قدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take the paired terms as good and evil deeds later acted upon by others, wealth given in charity versus wealth left by inheritance, endowment, or bequest, or the first and last deeds.
rows.anchor: أو بما قدم من حسنة أو سيئة وبما أخر من حسنة أو سيئة فعمل بها بعده أو بما قدم من مال تصدق به في حياته

rows.speaker: عبد الله الأنصاري
rows.claim: Abdullah al-Ansari urges repentance before death and sending wealth ahead as charity, since retaining it brings regret.
rows.anchor: عبد الله الأنصاري قدس سره

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says every person will meet the Lord without interpreter or veil, see only their own deeds on either side and Hell ahead, and should ward off the Fire even with half a date.
rows.anchor: ما منكم من أحد إلا سيكلمه ربه ليس بينه وبينه ترجمان ولا حجاب يحجبه فينظر ايمن منه فلا يرى إلا ما قدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is a clear witness against himself: his limbs testify to his deeds, so he already knows his condition and needs no outside informer.
rows.anchor: بل هو حجة بصيرة وبينة واضحة على أعمال نفسه شاهدة جوارحه وأعضاؤه بما صدر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine ending in basira can mark an emphatic noun, or the phrase can mean a perceptive eye, or a person possessing insight.
rows.anchor: أو عين بصيرة أو ذو بصيرة أو التاء للمبالغة كما في علامة ونسابة

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says the enduring, inscribed form of a person’s deeds remains within them and becomes the form of their qualities and limbs, so no external report is needed.
rows.anchor: بل الإنسان حجة بينة يشهد بعلمه لبقاء هيئة أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hal ata is a rhetorical question for affirmation and drawing the past near: hal means qad, while the implied hamza secures the listener’s admission; a real question of God is impossible.
rows.anchor: استفهام تقرير وتقريب فإن هل بمعنى قد والأصل أهل أتى أي قد أتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “a time” refers to the human species; because Adam was not made from a drop, the species means Adam’s descendants or includes him by generalization.
rows.anchor: والمراد جنس الإنسان لقوله من نطفة لأن آدم لم يخلق منها ثم المراد بالجنس بنوا آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the unspecified span of time as the nine months a person remains in the womb before becoming a human being mentioned among people.
rows.anchor: وهي مدة لبثه في بطن أمه تسعة أشهر أن صار شيئا مذكورا على ما ذهب إليه ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before becoming a mentioned human, the person was an unremembered drop in the loins; the pre-eternal world of spirits does not make one socially mentioned before embodiment.
rows.anchor: بل كان شيئا منسيا غير مذكور بالإنسانية أصلا نطفة في الأصلاب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر أو عمر
rows.claim: A report says Abu Bakr or Umar wept on hearing the verse and wished the unmentioned stage had continued, so that the person had never been created or charged with duties.
rows.anchor: أن الصديق أو عمر رضي الله عهما كما في عين المعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question makes resurrection undeniable to its rejecters: the One who brought a person into being after nonexistence can restore them after death.
rows.anchor: من أحدثه بعد أن لم يكن كيف يمتنع عليه بعثه وإحياؤه بعد موته

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says the person existed in divine knowledge and in reality through an eternal spirit, but was unmentioned among people while in the unseen.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني أي كان شيئا في علم الله بل في نفس الأمر لقدم روحه ولكنه لم يذكر فيما بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to obey a sinner or disbeliever warns the Prophet against Meccan pressure, including offers to stop preaching; even an innocent Prophet’s example shows people need repeated guidance against heedlessness and desire.
rows.anchor: وفي نهيه عليه السلام عن الإطاعة فيما يدعونه إليه مع إنه ما كان يطيع أحدا منهم ولا يتصور في حقه ذلك إشارة إلى أن الناس محتاجون

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani reads the sinner as one veiled by attributes or self from the Divine, and the disbeliever as one veiled by actions and their effects; agreement with them would veil the seeker too.
rows.anchor: ولا تطع منهم آثما أي محتجبا بالصفات والأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember the Lord from morning to evening, meaning continue remembrance at all times; the two times may also stand for Fajr, Zuhr, and Asr prayers.
rows.anchor: أي وداوم على ذكره في جميع الأوقات فاريد بقوله بكرة وأصيلا الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asil can extend from after Asr to sunset, or from noon onward, covering Zuhr and Asr.
rows.anchor: فكذا يطلق على ما بعد الزوال فيتناول وقتي الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti says a continuous-remembrance interpretation is needed only if the five prayers had not already been prescribed before this verse; he assumes they had been prescribed at the Ascension.
rows.anchor: وقال سعدي المفتي التأويل بالدوام إنما يحتاج إليه لو ثبتت فرضة الصلوات الخمس قبل نزولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi questions that assumption: the Ascension preceded the Hijra by a year, but the verse’s date is unknown, so the argument works only if it came afterward.
rows.anchor: وفيه إن الصلوات الخمس وإن فرضت ليلة المعراج إلا إن المعراج كان قبل الهجرة بسنة والتأريخ في نزول الآية مجهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “We” signals the majesty and collectivity of the Divine Essence, Names, and Attributes.
rows.anchor: النون للعظمة وللإشارة إلى جمعية الذات والأسماء والصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿṣirāt are clouds the winds are about to squeeze into rain; the imminence prefix means they are ready, not that the rain has already fallen.
rows.anchor: هي السحائب إذا أعصرت أي شارفت أن تعصرها الرياح فتمطر ولم تعصرها بعد فالإنزال من المستعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same imminence prefix appears in harvest-ready crops and a girl reaching puberty, supporting the sense “nearing the time.”
rows.anchor: يقال أحصد الزرع إذا حان له أن يحصد وأعصرت الجارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿṣirāt may alternatively mean winds about to squeeze out rain; the causative reading is unsuitable because the winds themselves are the squeezers.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد من المعصرات الرياح التي حان لها أن تعصر فتمطر فهي أيضا اسم فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thajjaj means abundant, successive flowing; the related hadith explains the pilgrimage’s loud talbiya and the pouring of sacrificial blood, while al-Zajjaj glosses it as pouring.
rows.anchor: والمراد تتابع القطر حتى يكثر الماء فيعظم النفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no conflict with rain being sent from the sky: it may descend through clouds, or arise through celestial causes such as the sun lifting water from earth and seas into clouds.
rows.anchor: فإن ابتداء المطر إن كان من السماء يكون الإنزال منها إلى سحاب ومنه إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entangled gardens symbolize gardens of love, mutual affection, and passionate longing, interwoven with one another.
rows.anchor: ألفافا جنة المحبة وجنة المودة وجنة العشق ملتف بعضها ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision is God’s division of creatures into the blessed and wretched according to differences and correspondences in their dispositions, forms, character, and deeds.
rows.anchor: فصل الله بين الخلائق وبين السعداء والأشقياء باعتبار تفاوت الهيئات والصور والأخلاق والأعمال وتناسبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its appointment belongs to God’s primordial knowledge and decree, before temporal time; the appointed moment of resurrection and recompense cannot be advanced or delayed.
rows.anchor: في علمه وتقديره الأزلي وإلا فثبوت المقاتية ليوم الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miqat is more specific than time in general: it is the fixed time when resurrection and the promised reward and punishment appear.
rows.anchor: فالميقات وهو الوقت الموقت أي المعين أخص من مطلق الوقت فهو هنا زمان مقيد بكونه وقت ظهور ما وعد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blowing clause explains the Day of Decision and magnifies it; the day is extended, with the blast at its start and judgment in the remainder.
rows.anchor: بدل من يوم الفصل أو عطف بيان له مفيد لزيادة تفخيمه وتهويله ولا ضير في تأخر الفصل عن النفخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israfil blows a second time on the luminous horn so spirits reconnect to bodies; “then you come” omits the intervening resurrection because the arrival at the assembly follows immediately.
rows.anchor: والصور القرن النوراني والنافخ فيه إسرافيل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People arrive in groups, either each nation with its leader or companies with differing conditions corresponding to their deeds.
rows.anchor: الجماعة المارة المسرعة أي حال كونكم أمما كل أمة مع أمامها

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muʿadh asked the Prophet about the groups; the Prophet wept and described ten classes of his community resurrected in grotesque forms, including monkeys, swine, and people dragged face-down.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ رضي الله عنه أنه سأل عنها رسول الله فقال عليه السلام : يا معاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marʿaha means pasture; water and grazing are attributed to the earth because they emerge from it, and this clause explains or completes the earth’s preparation for habitation.
rows.anchor: أي رعيها بالكسر بمعنى الكلأ وهو في الأصل موضع الرعي بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are grammatically governed by an implied verb explaining “anchored them”; they stabilize the earth only because God set them in place, not through an intrinsic property.
rows.anchor: منصوب بمضمر يفسر قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s provisions benefit people and livestock; grazing extends figuratively to everything consumed from the earth, even salt from water and fire from green wood.
rows.anchor: دل الله تعالى بذكر الماء والمرعي على عامة ما يرتفق به ويتمتع مما يخرج من الأرض حتى الملح فإنه من الماء

rows.speaker: العتبي
rows.claim: Al-ʿUtbi calls the mention of water and pasture a comprehensive expression for the earth’s food and useful products, including grass, trees, grain, fruit, salt, and fire.
rows.anchor: هذا أي قوله أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها من جوامع الكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of worldly provisions rebukes resurrection-deniers by comparing them to cattle that enjoy this life and forget the next.
rows.anchor: ونكتة الاستعارة توبيخ المخاطبين المنكرين للبعث وإلحاقهم بالبهائم في التمتع بالدنيا والذهول عن الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamma means to rise over and overwhelm; al-kubra describes greatness, not old age. The event is the overwhelming Resurrection or second blast, arriving soon after the temporary worldly provision.
rows.anchor: كل شيء كثر حتى علا وغلب فقد طم من باب رد والكبرى تأنيث الأكبر من كبر بالضم بمعنى عظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surahs’ use of al-tamma and al-sakhkha suits their order: if tamma is the first blast, it precedes the deafening second blast; if it is the second, both descriptions fit.
rows.anchor: بمعنى النفخة الأولى للإهلاك فهو قبل الصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day of remembrance explicates the great calamity; each person will see every good and evil deed recorded, though heedlessness and time had made them forget it.
rows.anchor: أي يتذكر فيه كل أحد كائنا من كان ما عمله من خير أو شر بأن يشاهده مدونا في صحيفة أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire shown to whoever sees is Hell generally, not one particular level; all can see it, including believers crossing the bridge, despite another verse mentioning its display for the wicked.
rows.anchor: والمراد مطلق النار المعبر عنها بجهنم لا الدركة المخصوصة من الدركات السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says only disbelievers see the fire, since believers will ask where the threatened Fire is and be told they crossed it while it was extinguished.
rows.anchor: وقيل للكافر لأن المؤمن يقول أين النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two outcomes answer what follows the great calamity: the transgressor is one who exceeds bounds in rebellion, exemplified by al-Nadr and his father al-Harith, and prefers fleeting worldly life over preparation for the lasting next life.
rows.anchor: أي فأما من عتا وتمرد عن الطاعة وجاوز الحد في العصيان كالنضر وأبيه الحارث المشهورين بالغلو في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the unbelieving transgressor’s permanent abode; believers who sin may leave it, so the passage addresses disbelievers while warning other readers.
rows.anchor: فالكلام في حق الكافر لكن فيه موعظة وعبرة موقظة واللام سادة مسد الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing the Lord’s station means fearing to stand before the Master for judgment on the great Day; such fear follows knowledge of creation and return.
rows.anchor: أي مقامه بين يدي مالك أمره يوم الطامة الكبرى يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى وذلك لعلمه بالمبدأ والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqam may be a verbal noun for standing, a place where servants stand for judgment and recompense, or an emphatic insertion.
rows.anchor: المقام إما مصدر ميمي بمعنى القيام أو اسم مكان بمعنى موضع القيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is paired with transgression because it is the first motive for obedience, followed by hope and then love; these suit ordinary people, the elect, and the most elect, respectively.
rows.anchor: جعل الخوف مقابلا للطغيان مع أن الظاهر مقابلته للانقياد والإطاعة بناء على أن الخوف أول أسباب الإطاعة ثم الرجاء ثم المحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restraining the self from desire means refusing natural appetites and worldly ornament because their consequences are harmful; hawa is desire without a religious warrant.
rows.anchor: عن الميل إليه بحكم الجيلة البشرية ولم يعتد بمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزهرتها ولم يغتر بزخارفها وزينتها

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet said his greatest fear for the community was desire and long hope: desire turns people from truth, while long hope makes them forget the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أخوف ما أتخوف على أمتي الهوى وطول الأمل

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: A great master says the seven desires listed in 3:14 reduce to worldly play and amusement, then to desire itself; escaping desire frees one from every bond and barrier.
rows.anchor: الهوى عبارة عن الشهوات السبع المذكورة في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says only prophets and some, not all, of the truthful escape desire; one is safe by imposing proper discipline on oneself.
rows.anchor: لا يسلم من الهوى إلا الأنبياء وبعض الصديقين ليس كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi describes the human as an isthmus between Divine and created, angelic and animal realities; from the higher aspect, a person restrains the lower self, as the Prophet addresses his human aspect from his angelic or unitive station.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان برزخ بين القحيقة الإلهية والحقيقة الكونية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Paradise alone is the person’s abode seems too exclusive if a sinful believer first enters Hell; Bursevi resolves this by taking the exclusivity to mean that whoever enters Paradise never leaves it.
rows.anchor: قد يدخل النار أو لا ثم يدخل الجنة فلا يصح في حقه الحصر

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani reads transgression as leaving human nature, justice, and religious law for animal or predatory states, and preferring sensory pleasures over real life; fear of God and restraining desire lead to Paradise according to one’s rank.
rows.anchor: فأما من طغى أي تعدى طور الفطرة الإنسانية وتجاوز حد العدالة والشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes the beginner seeking God renounce ease lest it veil him; the perfected person’s self, body, and devil become spiritual, so desire is transformed into the spirit’s single, true, acceptable pleasure.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم أشار بالآية إلى حال المبتدىء فإنه وقت قصده إلى الله لا ويجز له الرخصة والرفاهية خوفا من الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockers ask when God will establish the Hour; ayyan means “when,” and mursa is the fixing or establishing of its time.
rows.anchor: إرساؤها أي إقامتها يريدون متى يقيمها الله ويثبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a time cannot directly predicate an event, the grammatical estimate is “at what time is its appointed establishment”; the questioners mockingly invoke the Hour’s terrifying descriptions.
rows.anchor: فأيان ظرف بمعنى متى وأصله أي آن ووقت والمرسي مصدر بمعنى الإرساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What are you concerned with its mention?” rejects their request: the Prophet cannot tell them its time because that knowledge belongs exclusively to God.
rows.anchor: رد وإنكار لسؤال المشركين عنها وأصل فيم فيما كما إن أصل عم عما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s implied sense is that the Prophet has no knowledge of its time to explain to them; even the question’s premise that he could disclose it is denied.
rows.anchor: ما أنت من ذكرها لهم وتبيين وقتها في شيء لأن ذلك فرع علمك به وأنى لك ذلك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report from Aisha says the Prophet wanted to ask God about the Hour’s time, but was told its knowledge was not his and belonged to the Lord alone.
rows.anchor: عائشة رضي الله عنها فرموده كه حضرت رسول عليه السلام ميخواست كه وقت آن ازخدا بسد حق تعالى فرمود توازد انستن قيامت

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says knowing the Hour requires first effacing one’s own knowledge and then one’s self in God; the annihilated person has neither separate knowledge nor self to know it.
rows.anchor: أي في أي شيء أنت من علمها وذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s duty is to obey God by warning about the Hour’s nearness and terrors, not to assign a time that was never entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: أي وظيفتك الامتثال بما أمرت به مني بيان اقترابها وتفصيل ما فيها من فنون الأهوال لا تعيين وقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean either that the Prophet is only a warner, or that he warns only those who fear; the latter limits the effective response, not his mission to all.
rows.anchor: فهو من قصر الموصوف على الصفة أو ما أنت منذر إلا من يخشاها فهو من قصر الصفة على الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority treat “warner of those who fear it” as an adjective annexed to its object for brevity; fearers are singled out because they benefit from warning.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على إن قوله منذر من يخشاها من إضافة الصفة إلى معمولها للتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers, especially Meccan unbelievers, will think at the Hour that they had stayed only a single evening or morning after being warned.
rows.anchor: أي المنكرين وبالفارسية كوييا كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duha is the period from sunrise until noon; the short span refers to part of one day, with evening and morning linked by their belonging to the same day.
rows.anchor: الضحى اسم لما بين إشراق الشمس إلى استواء النهار ثم هي عشى إلى الغداة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abba may mean pasture from the root for intending or preparing, since animals seek it and it is readied for grazing; it may also be dry fruit prepared for sheep.
rows.anchor: أي مرعى من أنه آذا أمه أي قصده لأنه يؤم ويقصد جزه للدواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith about creation and provision from seven, then prostrating on seven, refers respectively to human developmental stages, listed kinds of food, and the seven prostration limbs.
rows.anchor: أراد بقوله خلقتم من سبع يعني من نطقة ثم من علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counted provisions run from grain through abba; gardens are excluded because they are where those foods grow, while prostration is on face, hands, knees, and feet.
rows.anchor: وبقوله فاسجدوا على سبع الأعضاء السبعة وهي الوجه واليدان والركبتان والرجلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, these blessings represent essential love, pure love from grapes, love of attributes, knowledge through dates and olives, lofty unity, ecstatic tastes, and gardens of longing; abba represents animal appetites.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى حب المحبة الذاتية وخمير المحبة الصافية المتخذة من عنب الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some spiritual gifts belong especially to the elite’s spirits, secrets, and hearts, while others are for ordinary human souls and natural faculties.
rows.anchor: مخصوص بالخواض كالأرواح والأسرار والقلوب وبعضها بالعوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deafening blast begins the account of the afterlife; the transition follows the short-lived provisions, and the omitted result of “when it comes” is that everyone becomes occupied with himself.
rows.anchor: شروع في بيان أحوال معادهم أثر بيان مبدأ خلقهم ومعاشهم والفاء للدلالة على ترتب ما بعدها على ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakhkha is the immense calamity to which creatures listen in their graves, namely the second blast; it may also be a cry so loud it deafens or a literal striking sound.
rows.anchor: لأن الناس يصخون لها في قبورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People turn away from relatives and do not ask about them because each is consumed by his own state and knows others cannot help.
rows.anchor: أي يعرض الإنسان عنهم ولا يصاحبهم ولا يسأل عن حالهم كما في الدنيا لاشغاله بحال نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list delays parents until after the brother because parents are closer, while attachment to spouse and children is stronger than attachment to parents; masculine wording includes women by Arabic convention.
rows.anchor: تأخير إلا حب للمبالغة لأن الأبوين أقرب من الأخ وتعلق القلب بالصاحبة والأولاد أشد من تعلقه بالأبوين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن طاهر الأبهري
rows.claim: Ibn Tahir al-Abhari says a person flees relatives after seeing their helplessness and would have relied on God alone in worldly life if he had recognized this truth then.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن طاهر الأبهري قدس سره يفر منهم إذا ظهر له عجزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward reading makes the heart flee its secret-brother, the self-mother, spirit-father, human faculties as spouse, and deeds and states as children; salvation comes through grace, not deeds alone.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى فرار مرء القلب عن أخيه السر وأمه لنفس وأبيه الروح

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says no one enters Paradise through deeds alone, including him, unless God envelops them in forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: لن يدخل أحدكم الجنة بعمله قالوا ولا أنت يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh explains that each person’s overwhelming concern fills the heart, leaving no room for another matter, like someone made wealthy by possessing much.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ أي الهم الذي حصل له قد ملأ صدره فلم يبق فيه متسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story in Farid al-Din Attar’s verse illustrates how shipwrecked travelers who share one plank still turn against each other under pressure.
rows.anchor: كشتى آورد در دريا شكست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven wandering planets are the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, each moving in its own sphere, with the Moon in the first.
rows.anchor: وهي الكواكب السبعة السيارة كل منها يجري في فلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawari means moving bodies and kunnas means hiding in a lair; the planets run in their spheres, then appear to retreat and hide beneath the Sun’s light, while Sun and Moon do not hide in that sense.
rows.anchor: الجواري جمع جارية بمعنى سائر والكنس جمع كانس وهو الداخل في الكناس المستتر به

rows.speaker: عين المعاني
rows.claim: Ayn al-Maʿani locates their retreat and concealment in their paths, as wild animals hide in their dens.
rows.anchor: لخنوسها في مجراها واستتارها في كناسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says all stars disappear from view by day and appear at night in their places, like animals emerging from lairs.
rows.anchor: وقيل جميع الكواكب تخنس بالنهار فتغيب عن العيون وتكنس بالليل أي تطلع في أماكنها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya reads the five planets as the five inner senses, the Sun as spirit, and the Moon as heart; the senses return to their stations and disappear beneath the two greater lights.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمة يشير إلى الحواس الخمس الباطنة السيارة مع شمس الروح وقمر القلب

rows.speaker: الوسيط
rows.claim: Al-Wasit takes asʿasa as night departing, since dawn rises as night withdraws and the order of mention follows their sequence in time.
rows.anchor: كان المناسب أن يفسر عسعس بأدبر ليكون التعاقب في الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asʿasa can also mean night arriving, one of the root’s opposite meanings; Bursevi finds this better matched to the paired dawn clause.
rows.anchor: أو أقبل فإنه من الأضداد كذلك سعسع وذلك في مبدأ الليل وهذا المعنى أنسب لمراعاة المقابلة مع قرينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanaffasa describes dawn as breathing, meaning the beginning of its rise.
rows.anchor: آنكاه دم زند يعني طلوع كند وتنفس أو مبدأ طلوعتس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars define shafaq as the red afterglow; when it vanishes, Maghrib ends and the time for Isha begins. Others define it as the white glow that follows, after which Isha begins.
rows.anchor: هي الحمرة التي تشاهد في أفق المغرب بعد الغروب وبغيبوبتها يخرج وقت المغرب ويدخل وقت العشاء عند عامة العلماء أو لبياض الذي يليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white-twilight view is one report from Abu Hanifa, though he is said to have returned to the majority view; the name suits both meanings because of their delicacy, especially the white light as the Sun’s glow weakens.
rows.anchor: ومن ثمة كان يفتي بالأول الذي هو قول الإمامين وغيرهما

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid interpret shafaq as daytime, understood as the Sun’s trace, so the oath covers night and day, the periods of rest and work that sustain the world.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة ومجاهد الشفق هو النهار بناء على أن الشفق هو أثر الشمس

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines twilight as daylight mixing with the darkness of night at sunset.
rows.anchor: وفي المفردات الشفق اختلاط ضوء النهار بسواد الليل عند غروب الشمس

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani reads twilight as the remaining light of human primordial nature after it sets into the body and becomes mixed with the darkness of the self; this light still permits spiritual perfection.
rows.anchor: أي النورية الباقية من الفطرة الإنسانية بعد غروبها واحتجابها في أفق البدن

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya sees twilight as an isthmus joining the unity of the night to the multiplicity of the day, and so as a manifestation of both Divine unity and the many Names.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن الله تعالى أقسم الشفق لكونه مظهر الوحدة الحقيقية الذاتية والكثرة النسبية الإسمائية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Night represents unity because sensible things disappear in it; day represents multiplicity because things become visible and varied livelihood fills it.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل الليل مظهر الوجدة لاستهلاك الأشياء المحسوسة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Wasaq is gathering scattered things; what night gathers includes animals and creatures returning to their shelters, or alternatively worshippers praying and seeking forgiveness before dawn.
rows.anchor: الوسق جمع المتفرق أي وأقسم بالليل وما جمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false dawn resembles a wolf’s tail and carries no legal ruling; the true dawn triggers fasting and prayer. Its emergence spreads light and sends people and animals out for provision, resembling resurrection.
rows.anchor: فجران مستطيل كذنب السرحان وهو الكاذب ولا يتعلق به حكم ومستطير وهو الصادق الذي يتعلق به الصوم والصلاة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi interprets dawn as the time when beloveds commune with God.
rows.anchor: سوكند بصبح كه وقت مناجات دوستانست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify dawn as the morning of Arafah, when pilgrims go to the plain and perform supplications, citing the report “Hajj is Arafah.”
rows.anchor: أو أقسم بصباح عرفة لأنه يوم شرف يتوجه فيه الحجاج إلى جبل عرفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn may instead mean the Day of Sacrifice, a great day for the required circumambulation, shaving, and stoning; it is reported as the greater Hajj day.
rows.anchor: أو صباح يوم النحر لأنه يوم عظيم أيضا ويقع فيه الطواف المفروض والحلق والرمي ويروى أن يوم النحر يوم الحج الأكبر

rows.speaker: التبيان
rows.claim: Tabyan offers further dawn images: the New Year, Friday as the poor person’s pilgrimage, miraculous water from the Prophet’s fingers or Moses’ stone, Salih’s she-camel from rock, springs, rain, or sinners’ tears.
rows.anchor: انفجار آب از أصابع حضرت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn imagery also urges repentance: if you carry a stain, wash it away with streams of tears.
rows.anchor: بران ازدوسر شمه ديده جوى ورآلايشى داري ازخود بشوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about night passing can mean travelers move through it; night protects them from heat and often from highwaymen, and the Prophet recommended night travel because the earth is folded then.
rows.anchor: يعني يسرى فيه الساري ويسير فيه السائر فإسناد السرى إلى الليل مجاز

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: When asked about the missing yā in “yasr,” al-Akhfash first had no answer, then explained that night is traveled through rather than traveling, so the form was altered to mark the shift in meaning.
rows.anchor: وسئل الأخفش عن حذفها فقال أخذ مني سنة فسأله بعد سنة فقال الليل يسرى فيه ولا يسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Night as it passes” swears by night’s passing, while the ten nights are sworn by without reference to their passage, so the two oaths are not redundant.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل القسم بالليل إذا يسر يغني عن القسم بليال عشر قلنا المقسم به في قوله والليل إذا يسر هو الليل باعتبار سيره ومضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the passing night can symbolize the self’s darkness disappearing as spirit is stripped bare, the absolute night of identity flowing into the day of determinate realities, or the Prophet’s supreme Night Journey.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى ظلمة الدن إذا ذهبت وزالت بتجرد الروح وإلى القسم بسريانه ليل الهوية المطلقة في نهار الحقائق المقيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about an oath for a possessor of intellect confirms the grandeur of the sworn signs and their worth as emphatic evidence; intellect is illuminated by knowledge of reality.
rows.anchor: تقرير وتحقيق لفخامة شأن المقسم بها وكونها أمورا جليلة حقيقة بالإعظام والإجلال عند أرباب العقول

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fath al-Rahman glosses the phrase as asking whether the oath is sufficient and adequate for a person of reason.
rows.anchor: وفي "فتح الرحمن" مقنع ومكتفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell need not be brought metaphorically: places can be brought in an instant by origination and annihilation; the expanded earth can contain Hell and the assembly, and its imaginal form may also appear, like Jerusalem shown to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لا حاجة إلى الحمل على التجوز فإن بعض الأمكنة كالكعبة تزور بعض الخواص بالإيجاد والإعدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person remembers failures by seeing their effects or embodied deeds, or finally accepts worldly guidance; the resulting regret is like repentance, but it is too late to benefit.
rows.anchor: أي يتذكر ما فرط فيه بتفاصيله بمشاهدة آثاره وأحكامه أو بمعانية عينه على أن الأعمال تتجسم

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says people then realize the truth contradicted their worldly beliefs: God appears in majesty and angels in the punishment their denial had earned.
rows.anchor: يوم يتذكر الإنسان خلاف ما أعتقده في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inserted question “how can remembrance help?” establishes that recollection and repentance after their proper time have no benefit.
rows.anchor: اعتراض جيء به لتحقيق أنه ليس بتذكر حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi argues that late repentance not being accepted shows there is no rational obligation to accept repentance; he then quotes al-Irshad’s objection that the verse proves nothing about repentance during earthly life and this recollection is not true repentance.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى لما نفى كون هذه الذكرى والتوبة نافعة له بقوله وأنى له الذكرى علمنا إنه لا يجب قبول التوبة

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad rejects that inference about repentance during worldly life: the remembered event is not repentance, since the person knows repentance must occur before death.
rows.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" والاستدلال به على عدم وجواب قبول التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker wishes he had sent good deeds ahead for the lasting, useful afterlife, or had performed saving deeds during worldly life; he wants work that keeps him among the living.
rows.anchor: يا ليتني عملت لأجل حياتي هذه يعني لتحصيل الحياة الأخروية التي هي حياة نافعة دائمة غير منقطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father and child may be Ismail and Muhammad, so the passage swears twice by the Prophet through his lineage; alternatively it is Adam and his descendants, which better fits the answer, or the shared human marvel of speech and form.
rows.anchor: وهو إسماعيل عليه السلام فإنه ولد بلا واسطة ومحمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of ma rather than man magnifies the wonder of what God produced, as in the phrase about what Mary’s mother gave birth to.
rows.anchor: وإيثار ما على من لمعنى التعجب مما أعطاه الله من الكمال كما في قوله والله أعلم بما وضعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands the father as the Prophet who taught the community its religion; a report to Ali calls the Prophet and Ali fathers of this community.
rows.anchor: وقيل الوالد أعلمكم أمر دينكم ولقوله عليه السلام لعلي رضي الله عنه أنا وأنت أبوا هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says every cause and lineage ends on Judgment Day except his cause and lineage, meaning religious connection and pious descent.
rows.anchor: بقوله عليه السلام كل سبب ونسب ينقطع يوم القيامة إلا سببي ونسبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is a father to believers because 33:6 calls him closer to them than themselves and calls his wives their mothers; a reading adds that he is their father, since a source of existence or repair can be called a father.
rows.anchor: وقد سمى الله النبي عليه السلام أبا للمؤمنين حيث قال النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet is from God and believers flow from his light; God also honored the community as a balanced nation and, in this reading, swore by them.
rows.anchor: وقد قال عليه السلام إنا من الله والمؤمنون من فيض نوري وصرح تعالى بفضيلة هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward readings identify father and child as Abraham-spirit and Ismail-secret, Adam-spirit and Abraham-secret, or the Holy Spirit and the rational soul; the Spirit is humanity’s true father.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى إبراهيم الروح الوالد وإسماعيل السر المولود منه أو آدم الروح وإبرهيم السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Holy Spirit reading echoes Jesus’ language about a heavenly Father and the command to imitate Him; the child is the human rational soul born from that spirit.
rows.anchor: أو إلى روح القدس الذي هو الأب القحيقي للنفوس الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabid originally describes an aching, swollen liver, then broadens to all hardship; humans are enveloped in toil from the womb through death and what follows.
rows.anchor: وأصله كبده إذا أصاب كبده كذكرته إذا قطعت ذكره ورأيته إذا قطعت رئته ثم اتسع فيه حتى استعمل في كل نصب ومشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fi suggests the person is surrounded by hardship as a vessel is by its contents; humanity undergoes successive pains from birth, circumcision, schooling, marriage, and children.
rows.anchor: ووجه آخر ن أقوله في كبد يدل على أن الكبد قد أحاط به إحاطة الظرف بالمظروف والمعنى لقد خلقنا الإنسان في تعب ومشقة
